title: Garden and Spire
premise: Quentin Ashgrove, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent years avoiding the wars that destroyed his order, guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains for coin and silence. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into his hands, Quentin discovers it charts the way to the Hollow Spire, where the king of Vaelmoor was bound thirteen turns ago and replaced by a hungry thing wearing his crown. Hunted by the crown's witch-hunters and shadowed by the courier's daughter, Wren, who wants the map for herself, Quentin must choose between the survival he bought with silence and the truth his oaths once demanded. In the end, Quentin unbinds the true king at the cost of his swordspeech — the magic that made him who he was — and finds that the found family gathered along the road is worth more than the power he surrendered.
about_author: Ivo Kavanagh is the pen name of a former cartographer's apprentice from the Welsh marches who now writes fantasy steeped in mountains, borders, and broken oaths. Their short fiction has appeared in several small-press anthologies, and 'Garden and Spire' is their first novel.

chapters.title: The Courier on Cold Larch Pass
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Guiding a smuggler caravan through Thornfell, Quentin finds a dying man clutching a sealed map, who presses it into his hands with a whispered warning about the thirteenth turn. The emotional beat is reluctant responsibility: Quentin wants to walk away, but an old oath stirs in his blood.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Studying the map in a border town, Quentin realizes it leads to the Hollow Spire and that the seal bears the royal sigil of Vaelmoor. Witch-hunters arrive asking questions. The beat is dread hardening into resolve as Quentin burns his old life's papers and slips out by night.

chapters.title: Wren of the Nine Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The courier's daughter ambushes Quentin on the mountain road, demanding her father's map; she carries half its cipher key tattooed on her arm. They fight, then bargain. The beat is prickly mutual need — two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: The Garden Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Following the map through a hidden valley, they find a ruined monastery garden where exiled swordspeakers once trained, and Quentin confronts memories of the order's massacre. A blind gardener, Mother Sable, joins them. The beat is grief finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Hunters in the White Silence
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Crown witch-hunters corner them on a glacier; Quentin uses forbidden swordspeech to save Wren, revealing what he is. She recoils, then chooses to stay. The beat is trust tested by truth and surviving its first fracture.

chapters.title: The City That Smiles Wrong
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Infiltrating the capital, they see the king at a festival — and notice how his shadow moves a heartbeat late. Courtier ally Ferro Bramble smuggles them into the palace archives. The beat is creeping horror beneath glittering normalcy.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns of the Moon
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. The archive reveals the binding ritual: the thing in the crown must be unbound before the thirteenth new moon, when the king's body will be consumed entirely. Betrayal strikes — Ferro sells their route to the hunters to protect his family. The beat is loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: The Road Through the Thorn
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Fleeing the capital with hunters behind them, the company crosses the smugglers' roads Quentin knows best, sacrificing supplies and safety for speed. Wren and Quentin finally speak honestly about fear and failure. The beat is found family forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Hollow Spire
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the spire, they face the crown-thing's guardian and descend to the bound king, who begs not to be freed — freedom means dying. Quentin must decide whether truth or mercy rules. The beat is the story's moral crux, held at knife-point.

chapters.title: A Garden Without a Sword
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Quentin unbinds the king using the last of his swordspeech, spending his magic like blood; the king dies human, and the crown-thing unravels. Wren, Sable, and a redeemed Ferro carry Quentin home to the monastery garden. The beat is bittersweet resolution: power lost, family gained, spring arriving in the ruins.
